texts.title: Create
texts.text:
You neet to create because a fulfilled life requires an active participant.
Consumption with no creative outflow, saving post for later & never actually implementing anything, ferments your potential and feeds your inner critic, which further continues this cycle of being scared to create and be seen creating, because you fear that others will judge you the same way you judge yourself, and also judge others.
Creating makes you honest & that honesty is what replaces judgement with understanding, because consumption raises your standard but creating anchors them with the cost of effort.
Create, if only to remind yourself that everyone is experiencing being a human for the first time, including you.

texts.text: Rituals can be defined as temporal technologies for housing oneself. They turn being in the world into being at home. Rituals are in time as things are in space. They stabilize life by structuring time. They give us festive spaces, so to speak, spaces we can enter in celebration.

Find your tree.
 Look for a tree that draws you in. It could be in a forest, park, or even your backyard. Trust your intuition.
Approach it with respect.
 Before touching the tree, please take a moment to greet it. Say hello silently or out loud. Approach slowly, with intention.
Hug the tree.
 Wrap your arms around the trunk or press your palms gently against the bark. Close your eyes.
Breathe and embrace presence.
 Inhale slowly, exhale deeply. Feel the texture of the bark, the strength of the trunk, the stillness of the moment.
Hug the tree as long as you need.
 You might stay for 30 seconds or 10 minutes. Let your body and heart guide you. Allow thoughts to drift by without clinging and invite your mind to be back to the hugging of your tree, here and now.
Express gratitude.
 Before you leave, whisper a thank you to the tree. You’re building a relationship with the natural world — one hug at a time.
